data.rationale: The fuzz harness (wolfmqtt-fuzzers/fuzzer.cpp LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput) drives wolfMQTT's client with attacker-controlled bytes returned by the mocked recv callback into the heap-allocated client->rx_buf (4096 bytes). The project is built with --enable-mqtt5, so the default protocol level is 5 and MqttClient_Connect -> MqttClient_WaitType -> MqttClient_DecodePacket -> MqttDecode_ConnectAck (mqtt_packet.c:803) reaches MqttDecode_Props with a buffer and prop_len taken directly from the wire. MqttDecode_Props loops while (prop_len > 0) but its per-type decode cases never check the remaining space (buf_len - (buf - pbuf)) before reading: MQTT_DATA_TYPE_BINARY (lines 563-577) reads a 2-byte length via MqttDecode_Num and advances buf by an attacker-controlled word16 (up to 65535) with no bounds check; MQTT_DATA_TYPE_STRING/STRING_PAIR call MqttDecode_String which reads buf[0]/buf[1] unchecked; MqttDecode_Num/MqttDecode_Int also read blindly. Once buf moves past pbuf+buf_len, subsequent iterations read past the end of the heap rx_buf, which ASAN reports as a heap-buffer-overflow READ. prop_len itself is not validated against buf_len either, so even short reads drift past the buffer end. The missing remaining-length validation in MqttDecode_Props is the root cause; callers pass correct buf_len but the function ignores it in every case except the two MqttDecode_Vbi calls.
